problem: For the function $f(x,y)=xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡y,$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(2,\pi ).$
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y) & =x(\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡y))+\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =x(1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡y))+\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =x(\operatorname{cos}⁡y-y\operatorname{sin}⁡y)+\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(2,\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(2,\pi )} & =2\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\pi \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\  & =2(-1-\pi \cdot 0)+(-1) \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$
